## Pull request overview

This PR removes the dedicated `ObjectManagerPage` and routes object management through the generic metadata management pipeline, adding a `listComponent` extension point to allow metadata types (like `object`) to supply a custom list UI while keeping the shared page shell.

**Changes:**
- Added `listComponent` to `MetadataTypeConfig` and taught `MetadataManagerPage` to delegate list rendering when provided.
- Introduced `ObjectManagerListAdapter` to integrate `@object-ui/plugin-designer`’s `ObjectManager` into the metadata pipeline.
- Unified entry points and legacy routes to `/system/metadata/object`, deleting `ObjectManagerPage` and migrating tests accordingly.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 13 out of 13 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments.

`MetadataObject` is imported as a type but never used, which will fail TypeScript compilation under `noUnusedLocals`. Remove the unused import (or use it if intended).
```suggestion
import { toObjectDefinition } from '../utils/metadataConverters';
```

`prevObjectsRef` is initialized from `displayObjects` once and never re-synced when `metadataObjects` load/refresh. If the initial render has an empty list (MetadataProvider starts with `[]`), the first user edit can compute an incorrect diff and persist the wrong object(s), potentially dropping changes. Sync `prevObjectsRef.current` with the latest `objects` when `localObjects` is null and `objects` changes (e.g., in an effect).

When `config.listComponent` is set, this component returns early, but the existing `fetchItems()` effect still runs and will call `metadataService.getItems(metadataType)` (and may toast on failure) even though the custom list is responsible for listing. Consider skipping the generic fetch/effect path when `listComponent` is present to avoid redundant requests and misleading error toasts.
